description: Uttar Pradesh has been a major epicenter of the Indian Freedom Struggle. From the Revolt of 1857 to massive peasant movements and revolutionary activities, the state deeply influenced the course of national history.

sections.title: First War of Independence, 1857
sections.description: The Revolt of 1857 ignited in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, and rapidly spread across Northern India.

historical_events.significance: An open rebellion by Indian Sepoys against the British East India Company, marking the official beginning of the 1857 revolt.

key_associations.extra_info: She led the revolt in the Awadh region and declared her young son Birjis Qadr as the Nawab.
They led a fierce armed rebellion against the British Army in Kanpur.
She fought valiantly against the annexation of her state under the Doctrine of Lapse and attained martyrdom.
Considered the fiercest enemy of the British during the revolt, he successfully utilized guerrilla warfare tactics.

sections.title: Peasant and Agrarian Movements
sections.description: Several large-scale agrarian movements erupted in Uttar Pradesh against exploitative British land revenue policies and oppressive Zamindars.

key_concepts.explanation: Formed in Pratapgarh in 1920, it was a massive peasant organization that strongly opposed arbitrary evictions (Bedakhli) and forced labour (Begar).
A unity movement started in 1921-22 in the northern districts of Awadh (Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur) against exceptionally high rent and oppression by revenue contractors.

key_associations.extra_info: He uniquely used recitations of the Ramcharitmanas to mobilize, inspire, and unite the illiterate peasants.
The movement was led by a lower-caste leader, transforming it into a highly powerful grassroots rebellion.

sections.title: Revolutionary Activities
sections.description: Uttar Pradesh was a prominent hub for revolutionary nationalism in India, witnessing numerous armed struggles for independence.

historical_events.significance: Mahatma Gandhi abruptly halted the Non-Cooperation Movement after an angry mob set a police station on fire in Gorakhpur, killing 22 policemen.
Members of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) executed a daring robbery of the British government treasury from a train near Kakori, Lucknow.

important_facts.fact: The Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) was founded in Kanpur in 1924 by revolutionaries Sachindra Nath Sanyal and Ram Prasad Bismil.
Chandrashekhar Azad attained martyrdom while fighting heavily armed British police at Alfred Park (now Chandrashekhar Azad Park) in Allahabad on 27 February 1931.

sections.title: Socio-Religious Reform Movements
sections.description: The 19th century witnessed the rise of crucial reformist and revivalist movements in Uttar Pradesh.

historical_events.significance: Launched to actively promote modern English education and scientific thinking among Indian Muslims.
An orthodox Islamic revivalist movement started in Saharanpur, which strictly opposed English education and western culture.

key_associations.extra_info: He founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College, which later evolved into the prestigious Aligarh Muslim University (AMU).
He co-founded the Darul Uloom Deoband seminary along with Rashid Ahmad Gangohi.

sections.title: Important Sessions of the Indian National Congress
sections.description: Uttar Pradesh hosted several historic and direction-setting sessions of the Indian National Congress (INC).

historical_events.significance: A historic session where an agreement was reached between the Moderates, Extremists, and the Muslim League. The session was presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar.

important_facts.fact: In the Kanpur Session of 1925, Sarojini Naidu created history by becoming the first Indian Woman President of the Indian National Congress.
In the Allahabad Session of 1888, George Yule became the very first English President of the Indian National Congress.
